children: Bahrain ranked first among Arab countries with a trade surplus of 33.2 per cent in the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 2025, according to recent data.

According to data based on figures from the World Trade Organisation and the International Monetary Fund, Bahrain recorded the highest trade surplus among the Arab countries included in the comparison, ahead of the UAE at 27.8pc, Libya at 24.1pc, and Qatar at 19.5pc.

A trade surplus of this scale means that Bahrain’s exports significantly exceeded its imports during the year, reflecting strong external-sector performance and the economy’s ability to generate positive net trade flows.
A trade surplus is generally considered a positive indicator.

However, Bahrain’s economic position cannot be assessed on this indicator alone, as foreign trade is influenced by several factors, including energy prices, the volume of exports and imports, re-exports, and the performance of non-oil sectors.

title: ZAWYA: Bahrain posts highest trade surplus among Arab countries
